item.title: DistroKid makes history by recognising maskandi, xigaza as official genres
item.description: Global music distributor DistroKid has officially recognised maskandi, a traditional Zulu music style, and xigaza, traditional xitsonga music, as distinct genres on its platform, marking a first in the international digital music industry. item.title: DistroKid, Spotify partner to support South African artists in digital music era
item.description: Global digital distributor DistroKid has entered a strategic partnership with Spotify to enhance access to digital music distribution and artist education across South Africa. The collaboration aims to support both traditional musicians and emerging independent artists across multiple genres, creating pathways for creators to share their work with global audiences. item.title: National Arts Merit Awards 2025 in Zimbabwe: All the winners
item.description: The winners of the National Arts Merit Awards (NAMAs) were announced at a ceremony held in Harare, Zimbabwe, on 28 March, recognising achievement across music, film, literature, visual arts and other creative disciplines. Music categories drew particular attention, with leading winners including Winky D and Jah Prayzah, winning two awards apiece. Winky D took home the Outstanding Music Video and People’s Choice Award while Jah Prayzah won the Outstanding Male Musician and Outstanding Album award

item.title: YouTube expands creator tools with voice replies, shorts remix features
item.description: YouTube has announced a significant expansion of its creator tools, making its voice replies feature available to all creators and introducing new AI-powered editing options for Shorts. The updates aim to enhance engagement between creators and viewers while fostering innovative content creation. The voice replies feature, first tested with select creators in December 2024, allows channel managers to respond to comments on their videos using voice recordings. item.title: Spotify introduces ‘Smart Reorder’ feature to enhance playlist transitions
item.description: Spotify has launched a new AI-driven playlist feature designed to improve transitions between tracks for Premium subscribers. The update, called Smart Reorder, automatically rearranges songs within a playlist based on their beats per minute (BPM) and musical key. The feature builds on Spotify’s custom transitions tool introduced last year, which enabled Premium users to create seamless transitions between songs. item.title: YouTube expands Premium Lite to include offline downloads, background playback
item.description: YouTube has expanded its Premium Lite subscription tier to include offline downloads and background playback, features previously reserved for the full YouTube Premium plan. The Lite tier, priced at $7.99 per month in the United States, now allows subscribers to download videos for offline viewing and continue watching content while using other apps or when their device screen is switched off. item.title: Open call: Arts and Cultural sector funding in Western Cape
item.description: The Department of Cultural Affairs and Sport (DCAS) has opened online applications for funding for the 2026/27 financial year. The call is open to registered arts, culture and heritage organisations, individual artists and events companies based in the Western Cape. Applicants must be South African citizens. item.description: The Gauteng Department of Sport Arts Culture and Recreation has issued a call for proposals for sport, arts and culture events or festivals seeking funding for the 2026/27 financial year, which ends on 31 March 2027. item.title: Downtown Music Publishing Africa to host publishing masterclass in Harare
item.description: Downtown Music Publishing Africa (SA) will hold a music publishing masterclass on 5 March 2026 in Harare, focusing on monetising music and collecting royalties through publishing and sync licensing. The session will take place at The Venue in Avondale, Zimbabwe, as part of Creative Economy Week. It is being organised in collaboration with Kay Media Africa and the British Council. item.title: Warner Music CEO flags AI and streaming deal updates
item.description: Warner Music Group CEO Robert Kyncl has outlined the company’s strategy to capitalise on artificial intelligence and recently renegotiated deals with digital service providers (DSPs) in a letter to shareholders.
